---
title: "Predict from a BayesR Fit"
---

## Predict from a BayesR Fit {.unnumbered}


### Description

Computes genomic estimated breeding values (GEBVs) and prediction
metrics. Works identically for full-fit, train/test split, and k-fold
CV — the caller is responsible for data partitioning; <code>predict()</code>
only evaluates the trained model on whatever data it receives.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>## S3 method for class 'masbayes_bayesr'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, y_new = NULL, X_new = NULL, ...)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="object">object</code></td>
<td>
An object of class <code>masbayes_bayesr</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="newdata">newdata</code></td>
<td>
Optional numeric design matrix. If <code>NULL</code>, the
training GEBVs (<code>object\$pred_train</code>) are returned.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="y_new">y_new</code></td>
<td>
Optional response vector for <code>newdata</code>. When supplied,
prediction metrics are computed.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="...">...</code></td>
<td>
Unused.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

Three usage modes:


<dl>
<dt><strong>In-sample (full-fit)</strong></dt><dd>Call <code>predict(fit)</code>. Returns
training GEBVs and the in-sample metrics already stored in the fit
object.
</dd>
<dt><strong>Forecast only</strong></dt><dd>Call <code>predict(fit, W_new)</code> without
<code>y_new</code>. Returns GEBVs for the new design matrix; metrics are
skipped.
</dd>
<dt><strong>Test evaluation</strong></dt><dd>Call <code>predict(fit, W_test,
    y_test)</code>. Returns test-set GEBVs plus <code>R2, RMSE, accuracy/AUC,
    bias</code>.
</dd>
</dl>

For test sets built with <code>construct_wah_matrix</code>, pass the
training matrix structure as <code>reference_structure</code> so that
<code>newdata</code> has identical columns to the training matrix.



### Value

An object of class <code>masbayes_prediction</code>: a list with
<code>GEBV</code> (liability scale for binary), <code>prob</code> (binary only:
<code>P(y = 1) = pnorm(GEBV)</code>, otherwise <code>NULL</code>),
<code>metrics</code> (<code>R2, RMSE, accuracy/AUC, bias</code> or
<code>NULL</code>; for binary, computed on the observed/probability
scale so <code>bias</code> is the calibration slope), <code>h2, sigma2_g,
  sigma2_e</code>, <code>variance_components</code>, <code>response_type</code>,
<code>model_type</code>, <code>eval_scope</code>, and <code>has_truth</code>.



### See Also

<code>run_bayesr</code>,
<code>summary.masbayes_bayesr</code>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masbayes")

# Train/test split
fit  <- run_bayesr(W_train, y_train, wtw_train, wty_train,
                   sigma2_e_init = var(y_train)/2,
                   sigma2_ah     = var(y_train)/2)

pred <- predict(fit, W_test, y_test)   # test-set evaluation
pred$metrics$accuracy
pred$metrics$RMSE

fc   <- predict(fit, W_unknown)        # forecast only, no y
fc$GEBV

insamp <- predict(fit)                 # in-sample reference
insamp$metrics$R2




```
